items.title: TRAI releases “The Telecommunication Interconnection (Port Charges) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026”
items.summary: 09 NOV 2026 4:24PM by PIB Delhi The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) today released “The Telecommunication Interconnection (Port Charges) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026” . These amendments introduce a framework for port charges for IP-based interconnection, supplementing the existing provisions applicable to ports for E1/TDM-based interconnection.

facts.text: Section 11(1)(b) of the TRAI Act, 1997, inter alia , empowers TRAI to prescribe the terms and conditions of interconnection between service providers, and to ensure technical compatibility and effective interconnection between different service providers.

To ensure that the existing regulatory framework governing interconnection matters remains relevant, transparent, and conducive to efficient interconnection between service providers, TRAI initiated a review of the regulatory framework through a Pre-Consultation Paper on the “Review of the existi…
Ceiling on annual IP-port charges : Annual ceilings on IP-port charges have been prescribed at ₹5.6 lakh per 1 Gbps IP port and ₹42.3 lakh per 10 Gbps IP port.

Graded framework for financial disincentives : For effective implementation of the regulations, a graded financial disincentive framework with a ceiling of ₹15 lakh per Service Area for each instance of contravention has been prescribed for contravention of specified provisions of these regulations.

facts.text: Under the aegis of the Department of Urban Development, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Swachh Survekshan (SS) Awards 2025-26 will honour India’s cleanest cities, celebrating their outstanding contributions to Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban.

At the launch event, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed to commence this initiative between all mentor and mentee cities.
